name: A10-0149/2026 – Bogdan Rzońca – Motion for a resolution (as a whole)
title: REPORT on the proposal for a decision of the European Parliament and of the Council on the mobilisation of the European Globalisation Adjustment Fund for Displaced Workers following an application from Belgium – EGF/2025/009 BE/Soliver
part_text:
The European Parliament approves giving Belgium 2,132,535 euros from a European fund that helps workers who lose their jobs. The money comes after the glass maker Soliver went bankrupt in December 2024, leaving 803 people without work in Flanders. The fund pays for job advice, training, help with job applications and job fairs. It covers 85 percent of the total cost of 2,508,865 euros. Parliament also asks Belgium to make the EU funding visible and to check later whether the measures worked.

- The EU releases 2.13 million euros to help 803 former Soliver workers in Flanders find new jobs.
- It affects the laid-off workers, many of them older and some with limited Dutch.
- Belgium runs the support until about two years after the decision takes effect.
